einzeiler: Comedian Brian Bates on turning anxiety and a resting worried face into comedy gold.
kurzfassung: Comedian Brian Bates discusses his new stand-up special "Worried," which streams on YouTube and was filmed in Nashville. He shares his journey from corporate television production to full-time stand-up following his father's passing in 2006. The conversation also covers his work on podcasts like The Public Figures and his minor role in Nate Bargatze's film The Breadwinner.
stichpunkte: Brian Bates's stand-up special "Worried" is executive produced by Nate Bargatze and available on the Nateland YouTube channel.
The special's title originates from high school when peers noted his natural expression and labeled him "worried."
Bates spent his early career working behind the scenes in broadcast television news in Nashville before pursuing comedy full-time.
He entered stand-up nearly twenty years ago after speaking at his father's funeral and discovering the healing power of laughter.
He co-hosts the Public Figures podcast alongside Aaron Weber and Dusty Sleigh, having previously spent six years on the Nateland podcast.
Bates plays "Trash Collector Number Two" in Nate Bargatze's theatrical film debut, The Breadwinner.
His stand-up material addresses everyday frustrations, parenting as an older dad, and relatable overthinking.

beschreibung:
What if laughter could truly be the best medicine? Join host Lynn Hoffman in this enlightening episode of Comedy Saved Me, where we dive deep into the healing power of humor with comedian Brian Bates. From the corporate grind to the spotlight of stand-up comedy, Bates shares his remarkable journey, revealing how he transformed personal struggles into relatable comedy that resonates with audiences everywhere. His new special, "Worried," tackles the intricate themes of anxiety, dating apps, and the quirks of everyday life, proving that the healing power of humor can be a lifeline during tough times.

As Brian Bates reflects on the profound impact of comedy in his life, especially following the loss of his father, he offers heartfelt stories that illustrate how laughter can be a source of resilience and emotional healing. This episode is not just an interview; it's a candid conversation about the intersection of comedy and personal triumphs, showcasing how comedy saved me and continues to uplift others. Bates shares anecdotes about his friendship with Nate Bargatze, who produced his special, and the joys and challenges of performing stand-up, making this episode a treasure trove of comedic advice and personal stories of comedy.

Listeners will appreciate Brian Bates and his unique perspective on parenthood and how his experiences as a father shape his comedic voice. With laughter as therapy, he highlights the importance of finding humor in life's challenges, making this episode a relatable and uplifting listen for anyone seeking comfort through comedy. The conversation flows naturally, touching on the broader themes of comedy and resilience, while also delving into the societal role of humor in navigating personal struggles.

If you’re looking for a dose of inspiration and laughter, this episode is a must-listen. Discover how comedy saved me and how it can offer solace and strength to those navigating their own journeys. Tune in to the Lynn Hoffman podcast for a heartfelt exploration of comedic storytelling, personal stories of comedians, and the undeniable connection between laughter and well-being. Whether you're a fan of blue collar comedy or seeking insights from the best comedic voices, this episode promises to deliver both entertainment and healing.

Join us as we celebrate the power of laughter with Brian Bates on Comedy Saved Me, where every joke is a step toward resilience and every laugh is a reminder of the joy in our shared human experience.
